name: io.github.benthepythondev00/socialblade-creator-stats
title: SocialBlade Creator Stats
description: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram & Twitch growth history from SocialBlade. Free/Pro keys or $0.01 x402.

tools.name: get_creator_stats
tools.description:
Follower or subscriber growth, history and suspicious spikes of YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and Twitch creators,
from SocialBlade's public pages (no login, 10-40 s).
Plan cost: 1 MCPize call (Free 100/mo, Pro $9/1,000, Business $29/5,000). Hard cap: max 10 profiles per call.
Set include_history=false for compact profile-only output.

Use it when a user asks how fast a creator is growing, what their subscriber or follower history looks like, how
two creators compare, or whether a channel had an unusual jump.

profiles: 1-10 creators, a mix of links and handles is fine. Accepted: a bare handle such as @mkbhd or khaby.lame
  (read on `platform`, default youtube; a YouTube channel ID UC... works too), the creator's own YouTube link
  (https://www.youtube.com/@mkbhd, /channel/UC..., /c/... or /user/...), a TikTok link (https://www.tiktok.com/@khaby.lame),
  an Instagram link (https://www.instagram.com/cristiano), a Twitch link (https://www.twitch.tv/shroud) or a
  SocialBlade link (https://socialblade.com/youtube/handle/mkbhd).
platform: youtube, tiktok, instagram or twitch; only used for bare handles, links carry their own platform.
include_history: true (default) keeps history, growth and spikes; false drops those fields and returns the profile
  numbers, grade and ranks only.
Examples: profiles=["@mkbhd"]; profiles=["@khaby.lame"], platform="tiktok";
  profiles=["https://www.youtube.com/@mkbhd", "https://www.tiktok.com/@khaby.lame"]

Returns one record per creator asked for, in the order given, each with input (as given), status and reason:
  status ok: the creator was read, reason is null and the fields below follow.
  status not_tracked: SocialBlade has no public profile for it (small or new creators often are not tracked).
  status blocked: SocialBlade could not be read for it this time (Cloudflare or time limit); try again later.
  status bad_link: not a creator profile link or handle.
When no creator comes back, the call returns an error that lists each input with its status and reason.
Platform note: Instagram returns current numbers and engagement rate without daily history (SocialBlade requires login for Instagram history).
Fields of an ok record:
  audience: audience_count (subscribers or followers, comparable across platforms), subscribers, followers, following.
  totals: views, videos, likes, average_likes, average_comments, engagement_rate.
  grade and ranks: grade (SocialBlade grade such as A+), sb_rank, audience_rank, views_rank, country_rank, category_rank.
  identity: platform, username, display_name, verified, country, channel_type, created_at, description, website_url,
    social_links, profile_url.
  history: a daily list (date plus audience, views and so on) of about 15 days, with history_days and history_from.
  growth: audience_gain_7d, audience_gain_30d, audience_gain_90d, views_gain_7d, views_gain_30d, views_gain_90d;
    a value is null when the history does not reach back that far (90 days is often null).
  spikes: audience_spike_dates and views_spike_dates, the dates whose daily gain was over three times the median,
    and spike_summary, the same in one plain line (e.g. "audience: 2 days with gains over 3x the median: 2026-10-14,
    2026-10-20"). It flags sudden jumps worth checking, not a fake-follower score.

platform.description: Platform for bare handles: youtube (default), tiktok, instagram or twitch. Links carry their own.

profiles.description: 1-10 creators: a profile link (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Twitch or socialblade.com) or a bare @handle / username on `platform`, e.g. ["@mkbhd"] or ["https://www.youtube.com/@mkbhd"].

include_history.description: true (default) returns the daily history, 7/30/90-day gains and spike dates. false returns the profile numbers, grade and ranks only: a smaller answer when you do not need growth.

tools.name: get_top_creators
tools.description:
Top creators from SocialBlade's public ranking lists, best first: YouTube worldwide, by country or by category
(e.g. the top 50 US gaming channels), plus TikTok, Instagram and Twitch lists (no login, 10-40 s).
Plan cost: 1 MCPize call (Free 100/mo, Pro $9/1,000, Business $29/5,000). Hard cap: max 100 creators per call via limit.

Use it to find creators to pitch, benchmark or track: "top 50 gaming YouTubers in the US", "most followed
Twitch streamers", "top German music channels by views". Follow up with get_creator_stats on any profile_url or
username for growth and history.

Examples: platform="youtube", category="games", country="US", limit=50; platform="tiktok", sort_by="likes".

Returns one record per creator in rank order: rank (1 is first), platform, username, display_name, profile_url,
audience_count (subscribers or followers), views, videos, likes, media_count, engagement_rate (Instagram), country,
channel_type (YouTube category), verified, created_at, avatar_url. Fields a platform does not list are null.
SocialBlade grade is not part of its lists; get_creator_stats returns it. An unknown category or country returns
no records; upstream failures return ToolError with HTTP status.

limit.description: How many creators from the top of the list, 1-100.

country.description: YouTube only. Two-letter country code, e.g. US, DE, BR. Leave empty for worldwide.

sort_by.description: Ranking measure. youtube: subscribers (default), views or videos. tiktok: followers (default) or likes. instagram and twitch: followers.

category.description: YouTube only. comedy, education, entertainment, film, games, howto, music, news, nonprofit, people, sports or tech. Leave empty for all categories.

tools.name: get_twitch_channels
tools.description:
Get Twitch channel profiles: followers, live status with viewers and game, partner or affiliate, team, social links and recent videos, from Twitch's public pages without login (3-20 s).
Plan cost: 1 MCPize call (Free 100/mo, Pro $9/1,000, Business $29/5,000). Hard cap: max 10 channels and 30 recent_videos per channel.

channels: channel names, @handles or twitch.tv links, e.g. ["shroud", "https://www.twitch.tv/pokimane"].
recent_videos: 1-30 recent videos per channel (default 5 for compact output).

Returns one record per channel: id, login, display_name, description, channel_url, followers, is_partner,
is_affiliate, team_name, social_links, is_live, stream_title, stream_viewers, stream_started_at, stream_game_name,
last_broadcast_game_name, profile_image_url and recent_videos (id, url, status, game_name).
A channel that does not exist returns no record; upstream failures return ToolError with HTTP status.

tools.name: get_bluesky
tools.description:
Read public Bluesky data (an account's posts, profile, followers or follows, or a post search) from Bluesky's public API (3-30 s).
Plan cost: 1 MCPize call (Free 100/mo, Pro $9/1,000, Business $29/5,000). Hard cap: max 10 handles/terms and max 50 records per call via limit.

mode: posts, profile, followers, follows (all need handles, e.g. ["bsky.app"]) or search (needs search_terms,
e.g. ["#python"]; Bluesky may refuse anonymous searches at times). include_replies / include_reposts apply to
posts. limit: 1-50 records in total.

Returns posts (uri, url, text, created_at, author_handle, like_count, repost_count, reply_count, quote_count,
images, external_link), or profile and follower records, depending on mode. Upstream failures return ToolError with HTTP status.

tools.name: get_instagram_videos
tools.description:
Get the direct MP4 links of public Instagram reels, video posts and carousels by link, without login (3-15 s).
Plan cost: 1 MCPize call (Free 100/mo, Pro $9/1,000, Business $29/5,000). Hard cap: max 10 post links per call.

post_links: reel, post or /tv/ links or bare shortcodes, e.g. ["https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeC12b5uha9/"].

Returns one record per link: status (ok when the post has a video; otherwise statusReason says why), shortCode,
postUrl, postType, ownerUsername, ownerFullName, isVerified, caption, takenAt, likes, comments, videoCount,
videoUrl (MP4 with sound), audioUrl (the sound alone), thumbnailUrl, durationSeconds, expiresAt (Instagram's links
expire after about 32 to 36 hours) and videos: one entry per video (slide number for carousels) with
originalWidth, originalHeight, hasAudio and qualities (label, width, height, bitrate, bytes, url; every rendition
up to 1080p, which has no sound: join it with audioUrl using ffmpeg). Upstream failures return ToolError with HTTP status.
